item.description: If the Houston Texans lose on Sunday, they might as well throw in the towel for 2026. Currently sitting at 2-5, the Texans must get back to their winning ways if they plan on making a postseason push. Right now, no one should be talking about the playoffs, especially since Houston has blown three fourth-quarter leads and remains winless at home. The Texans will travel to Los Angeles for a date with the winless Chargers in Week 9. The Bolts, who could be gunning for the No. 1 overall pick, fell short on Sunday in a battle of L.A. showdown against the Rams , where the offense mustered up nine points. The struggles continue for Justin Herbert in a year to forget. While only being sacked twice, the former top gunslinger threw for just 257 yards and threw a pair of interceptions. The Rams' offense could only muster 281 yards, but two touchdown runs from Blake Corum and Kyren Williams was the x-factor. As for Houston, it's coming off the bye week, though the roster could be in question at wide receiver once more. Second-year breakout star Jaylin Noel suffered a turf toe injury during the loss to the New York Giants in Week 7 and will miss the remainder of the regular season. The Texans could also be without starters Jalen Pitre and Reed Blankenship in the secondary, along with running back David Montgomery, who hasn't played in nearly a month. But where in the world will the Texans be on television? Is it only in Texas and California? Is the standalone late CBS game of the week? item.title: Slick Saints beat Prem Rugby Cup holders Leicester
item.description: Tom Rowe joined Northampton last season after scoring 23 tries for Loughborough Students in 2024-25 [Getty Images] Northampton kept their hopes of reaching the Prem Rugby Cup semi-finals alive after a dominant 39-19 derby victory over East Midlands rivals Leicester. A youthful Saints line-up turned on the style to sink the holders at Franklin's Gardens and stretch Northampton's run to 16 successive home wins in all competitions. Wings Tom Rowe and Amena Caqusau and full-back James Martin all touched down twice in a seven-try romp for the Saints. After three successive defeats in the Prem Rugby Cup, last season's winners Leicester are bottom of Pool B. It was not a perfect evening for Northampton. Already without two injured scrum-halves in England international Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland, the Saints lost a third in the 29th minute in Jonny Weimann. The 20-year-old, made captain for the evening, limped off after creating Northampton's first two tries, number one in the 11th minute with a glorious long pass to Martin and number two five minutes later with a cross-kick to Rowe. But England Under-18s scrum-half Sonny Goode showed Northampton's remarkable depth in the position with an impressive showing off the bench. After being steamrollered in a feisty Prem meeting at Mattioli Woods Welford Road a fortnight ago, this emphatic win provided a measure of revenge. Saints led 27-7 at the break with Rowe, Caqusau and centre Toby Thame also crossing. Caqusau produced a fine finish to secure the bonus point for Saints in the 36th minute and Rowe's second on the stroke of half-time gave Saints their 20-point interval advantage. But Martin went over for his second from a cross-kick in the 46th minute and then Caqusau added his second after some fine approach play by Goode with Leicester wing Adam Radwan in the sin-bin. Leicester, well beaten, managed three tries, two from hooker Sam Moli and one from back row Osian Thomas. Sale Sharks went to the top of Pool A with a tense 21-19 win over Bristol Bears at the CorpAcq Stadium. Two tries from Arron Reed - playing at full-back - and one from Alex Wills did the damage but Bristol took the game to the wire with two tries from Max Pepper after Totoa Auvaa, the Samoan hooker given a second chance by director of rugby Pat Lam following his sacking by Saracens for his off-field conduct, had opened their account. Sam Worsley had a chance to win it for the Bears four minutes from time but was short with a long-range penalty attempt.

item.title: In-form Thierno Barry leads Everton to a 3-1 victory over Coventry
item.description: Everton's Thierno Barry celebrates scoring his side's first goal during the English Premier League soccer match between Everton and Coventry City at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. (is associated with: «In-form Thierno Barry leads Everton to a 3-1 victory over Coventry») Peter Byrne/PA Wire/dpa Thierno Barry's hot streak fired Everton into the top five as they came from behind to beat Coventry 3-1. Only Manchester City striker Erling Haaland (nine) has more league goals this season after the 24-year-old's double turned things around against former Toffees manager Frank Lampard's side. Barry's rawness can be a source of frustration, as evidenced in the first half when he wasted a good chance to shoot by failing to get the ball out from under his feet, but he came alive inside the six-yard box after the break. Trailing to Yann Gboho's first goal for the Sky Blues in only his second league appearance, the Frenchman headed an equalizer before doubling his tally by bundling in a scrappy effort from barely two yards out. Lampard will argue his side should have had at least one penalty when James Tarkowski appeared to pull the hair of Caleb Yirenkyi with the score goalless in the first half, but their own defending left a lot to be desired. Barry has now scored in three successive games for first time for Everton and only second time in his career. He has six in his last seven in all competitions and 10 for the season - two more than he managed in his maiden campaign. Somewhat prophetically boss David Moyes, equalling Harry Catterick's record of 592 matches in charge, had said at his pre-match press conference that "Erling Haaland should be worried." And while realistically the Norway international will not be losing any sleep at the thought, Barry's form as the club's only recognized striker is proving a major boost. With Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall chipping in with goals from midfield, scoring the third nine minutes from time, to add to his all-round creativity Moyes is squeezing everything out of his limited resources. item.title: Why Max Verstappen ended F1 practice early in Brazil – Red Bull explains
item.description: Motorsport photo Max Verstappen finished Friday's Formula 1 practice sessions in Sao Paulo in third place. The Dutchman occupied that position in both sessions, in fact, and was also around two and a half tenths off the fastest driver in each session, with Lando Norris topping the first one and Kimi Antonelli the second. Red Bull concludes that there is once again "enough potential" in the car to fight at the front, although not everything went smoothly for Verstappen at Interlagos. During the first practice session of the day, he complained – as usual – about the downshifts, while a problem with the power steering gave him a "proper workout" towards the end of the session. Read Also: "Unacceptable downshifts" – Max Verstappen explains what's behind a recurring F1 radio complaint In second practice, Verstappen provided one of the most entertaining team radio exchanges of the F1 season so far when he did not immediately understand a message from Tom Hart – who is once again replacing Gianpiero Lambiase as his race engineer this weekend – about the power unit and gearbox. "So we have nothing on the switch, but they are adapting to you", Hart said over the team radio. It prompted Verstappen to respond in an almost sing-song voice: "What does that mean? I have to speak to the engine myself? I think I should be like 'oh, clutch, I’m switching! You’ll be punished otherwise!'" Too good, Max 😂 #F1 #BrazilGP @redbullracing https://t.co/FWaDrWZIRR — Formula 1 (@F1) November 6, 2026 More noteworthy was the fact that Verstappen ended the second practice session early. With just over six minutes remaining on the clock, the four-time world champion was already heading into the pitlane, apparently at his own suggestion, judging by the team radio exchanges. Verstappen suggested coming in, to which Hart replied: "Okay, Max. If you want to box, then come in at the end of this lap. Radio has gone poor, for info." At the end of the practice day in Sao Paulo, Red Bull's head of race strategy Hannah Schmitz explained why Verstappen had returned to the pits early: "So it was just [because of] finding a lot of inconsistencies in the long run and we didn't feel like it was helpful anymore. "We weren't getting the data we needed. We knew the things that we wanted to be looking at and changing overnight, so we just went straight into that." That is particularly noteworthy, as coming in early also meant Verstappen gave up the opportunity to carry out a practice start on the grid. Given that the grid at the Autodromo José Carlos Pace slopes quite steeply uphill and Red Bull's starts have not always been particularly good this year, that is remarkable. After Verstappen got out of the car, mechanics were seen working underneath his RB22. item.title: Keenan's hat-trick inspires Ireland to rout of Argentina
item.description: Ireland full-back Hugo Keenan scored three tries as as the Irish routed Argentina 42-12 (Paul Faith) Hugo Keenan scored three tries in his first home Test appearance in over a year as Ireland outclassed a disappointing Argentina 42-12 in their Nations Championship match on Friday. The Irish ran in six tries to get their November campaign in Dublin underway in impressive fashion. They go on to play Fiji on Saturday week before the biggest challenge, world champions South Africa in a fortnight. Ireland go top of the Nations Championship northern hemisphere standings ahead of the rest of the matches this weekend. Argentina stay fourth in the southern hemisphere table. They next play Italy and France. Irish rugby legend Fergus Slattery and Ireland's 2024 European 1500 metres champion Ciara Mageean were honoured with a minute's applause prior to the national anthems. Argentina broke the deadlock in the 11th minute -- Tomas Albornoz sent a delightful crossfield kick into the try area and it was no contest between Pumas wing Mateo Carreras and the smallest player on the pitch Craig Casey. Albornoz failed to convert to leave Argentina 5-0 up. The Irish though struck back with a stunning try, Casey getting back into Andy Farrell's good books as he forced a turnover penalty. Right wing Rob Baloucoune popped up in the centre and burst through the Argentina defence, passing to Mack Hansen, who offloaded to Keenan. Keenan, like Hansen returning after a long absence from the Test side because of injury, finished it off -- Sam Prendergast converted for 7-5. The hosts put together another polished move to score their second try, flanker Nick Timoney pierced the Argentinian defence and got to within metres of the line. Hooker Dan Sheehan had started the move and appropriately finished it off -- crashing over for the try. Prendergast converted for 14-5. The Irish were fully into their stride by this stage, and try number three came soon afterwards. It was a quite brilliant individual effort from Keenan, taking the pass from Hansen, who had come off his wing, and beating three Argentina players to touch down. Prendergast converted for 21-5 at the half hour mark -- Argentina's early fire well and truly doused. - Montoya blow - Pumas new defence coach Shaun Edwards looked on ruefully from the box high up in the stands. A further blow came with captain Julian Montoya failing a Head Injury Assessment (HIA) and would not be returning -- referee Luke Pearce had to inform a surprised Pablo Matera he was now skipper. Argentina were firmly on the back foot and their ill discipline, which has been a problem all year, let them down as the Irish forced them into conceding penalty after penalty. item.title: Bill Simmons has insatiable thirst for watching Joe Buck and Troy Aikman broadcast through hatred
item.description: Credit: ESPN and The Bill Simmons Podcast Joe Buck and Troy Aikman might not love each other, but they should feel the love from Bill Simmons, who can’t get enough of their “mutual hatred” on Monday Night Football . By now, everyone knows Buck and Aikman had a blowup before a Monday Night Football broadcast last month stemming from their differing contract situations with ESPN. Aikman remains headed for free agency with ESPN appearing to have no serious interest in retaining him, while Buck quietly agreed to a long-term extension with the company last May. And in the wake of the reported blowup, all eyes and ears have attempted to decipher whether the feud is spilling onto the broadcast. During Friday’s mailbag portion of his podcast, Simmons read a note from a listener who claimed watching Buck and Aikman on Monday Night Football is getting too uncomfortable amid their reported feud. @BillSimmons can’t get enough of the Troy Aikman–Joe Buck tension on ‘MNF’ https://t.co/Zx1XXeKbwA — The Ringer (@ringer) November 6, 2026 “I feel completely the opposite. I love it,” Simmons insisted. “I love it, I want them to stay together and just be in mutual hatred.” Simmons proceeded to mimic the Monday Night Football opens since their reported blowup, where Aikman now appears to be staring into the abyss as Buck welcomes the audience with his monologue. “He looks like somebody is in his earpiece giving him the worst news possible about the stock market that day, or that his crypto account got wiped out,” Simmons continued. “I love it, I don’t want them to breakup. Keep them together.” ESPN probably isn’t as enamored with the feud as Simmons is. But the question is whether ESPN views this as an “any publicity is good publicity” situation, or if the network is getting concerned this rift could eventually grow to the point where Buck and Aikman are unable to work together? Many sports fans have shared Simmons’ curiosity over how the Buck and Aikman situation will play out. And considering nobody has been arrested or committed any offense worthy of being fired, it’s fair to wonder whether ESPN is welcoming the added attention to an extent. Simmons is likely to get his wish of watching this continue. Unless Aikman starts publicly badmouthing Buck and the company beyond what’s been reported, ESPN isn’t going to make an in-season change, especially as they prepare for their first Super Bowl broadcast in three months. They’ve got another big game this weekend as they attempt to dig themselves out of the NFC East’s basement and catch up to the division-leading Giants in a down year. The Los Angeles Rams are coming to town, and they’re bringing a freshly-activated Myles Garrett with them. It’s been a disappointing 4-4 start for a team that was on a lot of people’s predictions to win the Super Bowl. Washington is 2-4-1 for the season, and this is another critical game for a team that’s two games behind in the division. The Rams have been disappointing to preseason expectations, but they are still a good team that opened as 5.5-point road favorites. Matthew Stafford was the NFL’s MVP last season, but he’s been throwing interceptions at a higher rate this year. Davante Adams is out, but Puka Nacua will be on the field testing a secondary that looked better against the lowly Eagles. The Washington Commanders will be missing two more weapons on Sunday afternoon with Treylon Burks (foot) and Dyami Brown (calf) ruled out on Friday. There are only two healthy receivers who have caught passes from Jayden Daniels this season in Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams. Players like Luke McCaffrey, Van Jefferson, and possibly Jaden Bradley could see their number called more this week. TE Chig Okonkwo has been a big factor since returning from injury, and he will be a top-2 receiving option vs the Rams. The Commanders running backs room continues to change due to injury. Jeremy McNichols returned from IR, but quickly went back on the reserve due to a new foot injury. That led to the Commanders claiming rookie Robert Henry Jr off waivers, a return after the Seahawks did the same a month ago. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler are the only other healthy backs on the 53-man roster. Washington continues to look for a run game that hasn’t materialized this season. Will Ekeler get more snaps this week or can the new blood pump some life into the ground game this week? This game’s 47.5 O/U lines up with our predictions this week, but hopefully the scores are switched and the Commanders pull off the upset. I’m taking the under here, and I think the Commanders won’t be able to overcome the injuries this week. Matthew Stafford will have a pick or two, but he’ll also target Puka Nacua 14+ times for a big day. The Commanders run game, or lack there of, continues to hold the offense back, and put too much on Jayden Daniels. Look for a big rebound next week in a true make-or-break game for the Commanders. item.title: Will England Say Alright to Ben White?
item.description: Will England Say Alright to Ben White? Six Gunners could be representing England in the next international break. They would have possibly equalled the record of seven had Saka not been injured. A lot might depend on whether Thomas Tuchel chooses to recall Ben White. The manager has said how unlucky the defender has been with his timing, often on the sidelines just at the moment the German is selecting a squad. That seems to hint that, if fit, the 28-year-old would have added to his six caps, but also carries the warning that the window is getting smaller with every camp that is missed. Can Ben White Win Over England Supporters? Many English fans won’t sympathise with the player due to him choosing to return home early from the 2022 World Cup and, for the rest of the Southgate era, asking not to be considered for selection. Rumours have since ranged from a clash with the coaching staff, feeling homesick or not being able to socialise with his peers as reasons he made himself unavailable. The man himself has never made it public why he didn’t want to represent his country for a while. The right-back has been fortunate that, in his absence, the role has become a problem position for his nation. Five different individuals were utilised at RB during the last World Cup, so you assume a 100 per cent fit White would have been on the plane to North America? Especially when you consider his versatility. As we’ve previously discussed regarding White’s return to international football under Tuchel , his England future has been a talking point for some time. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Could Arsenal’s Rotation Help White’s England Chances? It’s been a few seasons now since White didn’t have some sort of niggle, and you sense Mikel Arteta doesn’t feel comfortable starting him every few days? That would be an issue in terms of the next Euros, but he could be an option in the squad. His competition at Arsenal is Timber, but that’s worked out perfectly for both. The Dutchman has his own history. Our manager has recently rotated his full-backs every few days, something that makes sense given the injury problems both White and Timber have experienced . If Timber plays on the Sunday, White plays on the Wednesday, so I assume it’s Timber’s turn to play against Hull. That lets both defenders have their minutes managed while getting enough playing time to stay in contention for their nations. Stay healthy and a spot in the Three Lions’ XI could be up for grabs? item.title: Arteta shares more detail on Saka’s injury and dismisses Declan Rice concern
item.description: Arteta shares more detail on Saka’s injury and dismisses Declan Rice concern Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta admits there is still significant uncertainty over Bukayo Saka’s injury, including exactly what caused it and when the winger will be ready to return. Saka is expected to be sidelined for several weeks , but Arteta stressed Arsenal are still trying to understand the problem and are reluctant to put a firm timeframe on his recovery. “There are a few things that we believe can contribute but I prefer not to mention that here,” Arteta said on Saka’s freak quadriceps injury, which he suffered while passing the ball against Bayern Munich. “In reality, to put your finger on something, maybe after you are totally wrong and it’s something else, so it’s very difficult. “We have obviously openly discussed a lot of things with him to understand what could possibly have gone wrong but the reality is probably that, unfortunately, we don’t know. “We can think that it’s that but nobody has certainty.” Asked whether Saka could be out for around a month, Arteta said: “I think so, but I don’t know. “The way it happened, it wasn’t a really aggressive action. So that gives you some hope as well that the tissue will repair in a more efficient and faster way as well. “He’s had some very good symptoms right now so we have to wait and see.” Arteta also dismissed concerns over Declan Rice’s workload, insisting Arsenal have taken particular care in managing the midfielder. “He’s the only player in the squad that for two games in the Carabao Cup has been left out of the squad, at home with two days off,” Arteta said. “It’s not true. We are really looking after him. More than any other season, in training and all the load. “He is at the demands of this football club and not only him because there’s many others who have had even less time off. “That has to be the mindset and if you start to put other things in your brain, damage. Erase them, put them in the bin, and just focus on what you have to do.” Stay up to date with all the latest Arsenal news by joining our Arsenal WhatsApp channel .

item.description: NEW ORLEANS - JANUARY 4: Head coach Nick Saban of the Loiusiana State Tigers stands next to the Bowl Championship Series Trophy after his team defeated the Oklahoma Sooners in the Nokia Sugar Bowl National Championship on January 4, 2004 at the Louisiana Superdome in New Orleans, Louisiana. The Tigers defeated the Sooners 21-14 to win the National Championship. (Photo by Brian Bahr/Getty Images) | Getty Images What are you reading this article on? If you are reading this on an Apple device, you are holding ultimate proof that winning one out of three fights can still change history. Early on in the years of the personal computer era, Microsoft dominated the market while Apple was still operating out of the garage of Steve Jobs’ parents. Apple did not survive by trying to replicate what Microsoft was doing; it decided to change the game entirely. Apple released the iPod in 2001 and the iPhone in 2007, paving the way to overtake Microsoft in technology sales and define the history of technology. LSU and Alabama are not too different in this dynamic. LSU’s .328 win percentage against Alabama is much worse than a coin flip, but it is not full-on submission. Alabama boasts the win percentage, but LSU has the ability to create culture-shifting runs like 2019 that will forever be the measuring stick for any really good team in college football. LSU and Alabama first played in 1895, with the Tigers taking a 12-6 victory. Since then, Alabama has taken command of the series, with a 58-27-5 record. For LSU, this is always a game that carries a lot of weight since every National Championship LSU has won or participated in has come with a win over Alabama in the regular season. It was already a heated rivalry, but Nick Saban switching sides poured more gas on the fire. Saban, while at LSU, was 4-1 against the Crimson Tide, with the lone loss coming in 2002 when the Tide came into Baton Rouge and shut out the Tigers 31-0. Brodie Croyle was the quarterback for Alabama, completing 12 of his 33 passes for 154 yards with one interception thrown to Chad Lavalais. A dominating performance that led to LSU defeating Oklahoma in the Sugar Bowl for the National Championship. item.title: When and how did the BYU-Utah football rivalry game become must-see TV for entire nation?
item.description: BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier (47) jumps over Utah defensive tackle Pupu Sepulona (45) and Utah cornerback Elijah Davis (9) during a run into the endzone for a rushing touchdown as BYU and Utah play at LaVell Edwards Stadium in Provo on Saturday, Oct. 18, 2025. | Scott G Winterton, Deseret News One of the most memorable games in the century-old BYU-Utah football rivalry — at least for BYU fans — was played 20 years ago this month. After taking an early 14-0 lead, then falling behind 31-27 late in the fourth quarter at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City, the Cougars won 33-31 on a touchdown pass from John Beck to Jonny Harline with no time remaining on the clock. As the Bronco Mendenhall-led Cougars raced onto the field to celebrate the finish that became known, simply, as “Beck to Harline,” the pro-Utah crowd sat in stunned silence . That BYU didn’t attempt to kick an extra point to make the final score 34-31 was somehow appropriate, because twice in the 1990s, the Utes had defeated the Cougars by that 34-31 score, prompting a series of television commercials featuring BYU coach LaVell Edwards and Ron McBride that added to the allure of the matchups. Speaking of television, that instant classic in 2006 was not televised nationally on a major broadcast network. Instead, it was broadcast regionally via CSTV (College Sports Television) and shared regionally on The Mtn. (MountainWest Sports Network). Television ratings for the game were not known because The Mtn. did not subscribe to Nielsen Media Research tracking. Flash-forward to Saturday morning at 10 a.m. at Rice-Eccles , when millions are expected to tune in to ABC for the first top-10 clash in rivalry history. What was once an in-state and regional obsession, a grudge match that was one of the best-kept secrets in the Beehive State, has become must-see TV nationally. The rivalry began capturing more of the nation’s attention when Utah went to the Pac-12 in 2011 and BYU went independent and signed a deal to get its home games televised by ESPN, but Saturday’s game might never be matched in terms of national attention. Although there are six other games pitting ranked teams on Saturday, No. 3 Utah hosting No. 9 BYU on a national television network feels like a seminal moment for the rivalry. item.description: While looking at the modern era of college football, Georgia coach Kirby Smart said athletes are facing “an all-time high of mental stress” amid mounting outside pressure. With that, he called on schools to provide more support on that front. Smart cited the amount of pressure that comes with the NIL era, in particular. He added pressures they currently face are different than those he and others had during their careers. “I think these kids are at an all-time high of mental stress,” Smart said Thursday on his radio show . “They have stressors at home. A lot of them make NIL money that’s large money for a college athlete. But on the flip side, Kirby Smart noted they can also hear more of the criticism that previous generations were able to avoid. That could also have an impact on an athlete’s headspace and add to what they’re dealing with off the field. “They’re comparing themselves to others,” Smart said. “They’re looking at what people say about them. item.title: WTA chair apologises to Pegula for airing of 'diva' comment
item.description: Jessica Pegula is a member of the WTA players' council [Getty Images] Women's Tennis Association chair Valerie Camillo has apologised to Jessica Pegula and said the live-streaming of private comments to her coach about fellow player Mirra Andreeva was "regrettable and unacceptable". American Pegula called Andreeva a "diva" in a private conversation with her coach after a practice session for the WTA Tour Finals on Wednesday. However, the comments were aired on a live stream after the WTA failed to tell players there were microphones on practice courts. World number five Pegula called the incident "unfortunate" and said the WTA players' council supported players' calls for more privacy. Camillo said that all audio recording equipment in practice areas had since been removed as "clearly there was a failure in our technical execution and monitoring". "I want to specifically apologise to Jessica Pegula and [coach] Mark Knowles," she added. "What happened was regrettable and unacceptable. Jess is one of the WTA's best advocates and biggest stars. She does not deserve this distraction." WTA takes responsibility after Pegula 'diva' comment live-streamed Pegula was also heard saying French Open champion Andreeva "needs to be humbled" and her coach Conchita Martinez encourages her behaviour. A representative for Pegula said she had been in direct contact with those involved and had been "completely unaware" the conversation could be heard by courtside microphones. None of the players were asked about the incident in the pre-tournament news conference at Indian Wells on Friday, but Pegula did address it in an interview with ESPN. "I think it's something that we have fought a lot over the last couple years as there's a lot more surveillance and audio and access to the players at tournaments than there has been in the past," she said. "I know for broadcasting that it's great for fans, but I think we've seen a couple incidents now throughout the year, [the] last couple of years really, where it just seems highly unnecessary. "I think [this will] definitely reignite the topic and, hopefully, we can unfortunately use this incident to keep pushing for more player privacy." Pegula's compatriot Coco Gauff called for more privacy after she was captured in the players' area smashing a racquet following a defeat by Elina Svitolina in the Australian Open quarter-finals in January. item.title: Former Celtics Champion Makes Major Announcement About His NBA Future
item.description: Former Celtics Champion Makes Major Announcement About His NBA Future originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kristaps Porzingis is stepping away from basketball as he prioritizes his health, leaving his NBA future uncertain. The former Boston Celtics center shared an official statement Friday announcing his decision after his body did not respond as he expected while ramping up for the 2026-27 season. 🙏🏼 https://t.co/d0UoELOmye — Kristaps Porzingis (@kporzee) November 6, 2026 Porzingis made it clear that he had hoped to play alongside his current group this season but does not believe he is physically ready to perform at the level he expects of himself. The announcement follows several weeks of uncertainty surrounding Porzingis' availability with the Golden State Warriors. He has yet to appear in a game this season after being ruled out indefinitely because of a health issue. He also missed significant time last season, appearing in just 32 games between the Atlanta Hawks and Warriors. Porzingis' statement did not officially declare his retirement, but it raises questions about whether he will play in the NBA again. The 31-year-old also acknowledged his situation with Golden State, saying he wants to show respect for the organization and work with the Warriors to find a solution that makes sense. His announcement comes after reports surfaced that Golden State was exploring potential trade options involving the veteran center. The Warriors also reportedly stopped making payments on his $20 million salary while he remains away from the team. Porzingis is on a trade-flexible contract for $20 million this season and a small partial next year, serving as essentially an expiring deal that the Warriors can utilize, potentially with their pool of assets. He first revealed his POTS diagnosis last year and has had ups and downs with the issue. If there is no breakthrough in recovery, stepping away from basketball -- for good -- is possible. — Shams Charania (@ShamsCharania) October 21, 2026 Porzingis joined Golden State ahead of the 2026-27 campaign after spending part of last season with the Warriors following a midseason trade from Atlanta. His NBA career has included stops with the New York Knicks, Dallas Mavericks, Washington Wizards, Celtics, Hawks and Warriors. He became an All-Star with New York in 2018 before eventually finding championship success in Boston. The Celtics acquired Porzingis in a three-team trade ahead of the 2023-24 season. He played a significant part in Boston's championship run, averaging 20.1 points and 7.2 rebounds per game during the regular season. Although injuries limited his availability in the playoffs, he helped the Celtics capture their 18th NBA championship in 2024. Porzingis' latest announcement puts his playing career on hold as he focuses on his health. Whether that means the end of his NBA career remains to be seen.
